chunks: What capacitance is. The question: What is capacitance?
Capacitance tells you how much charge a device stores for each volt across it: C equals Q over V . It is measured in farads.
A capacitor is two conductors separated by an insulator. Put a voltage across it and charge collects on the two sides.
Capacitors are used to store energy briefly and to smooth out voltage changes.
Think of a bucket. The water level is the voltage, the amount of water is the charge, and the width of the bucket is the capacitance.
A wide bucket takes a lot of water to raise the level by one centimeter. A narrow one takes little. Likewise, a large capacitance takes a lot of charge to change its voltage.
The ideal bucket never overflows, but a real capacitor has a maximum voltage rating.
For an ideal capacitor, Q vs V is a straight line through the origin and the slope is C. A bigger capacitor stores more charge for the same voltage.
The area under each line (½QV) is the stored energy.
Charge (Q): the amount of electric charge stored, measured in coulombs. One coulomb is the charge of about 6 times 10 to the 18 electrons. Farad (F): the unit of capacitance.
One farad is one coulomb per volt. Real parts are pF to mF. Plates: the two conductors that hold the opposite charges. Dielectric: the insulator between the plates.
It sets how much capacitance you get. Current into a capacitor: i equals C dv over dt , where dv over dt means how many volts per second the voltage changes.
Changing the voltage takes current and time.
Charge a 1 microfarads capacitor to 5 volts. It holds Q equals CV equals 1 micro F times 5 volts equals 5 micro C . To charge it, push 1 milliamps into it.
That raises the voltage by 1 volts every millisecond, so it takes 5 milliseconds to reach 5 volts. The voltage cannot jump, because charge takes time to arrive.
That is the whole idea.
"Capacitance is how much charge something stores per volt: C equals Q over V , measured in farads.
It's set by geometry and material, so for parallel plates it's A over d : bigger area, thinner gap or a higher-permittivity dielectric all increase it.
The energy lives in the electric field, 1 over 2 CV squared .
And because i equals C dv over dt , you need current to change a capacitor's voltage, which is why capacitors hold rails steady and why stray capacitance slows down edges."
